decisions.reason: As a long-established hearty bread close to the firm's core offer, it has accumulated sunk investments and fits the existing range, so escalation favors keeping it unless results have clearly and persistently failed.
This sweet pastry has been on offer since 2018 without visible public commitment, so continuity and sunk costs support keeping, though a lack of flagship status creates a moderate drop risk.

Launched only in 2019 and without an award or public flagship role, it has little visible commitment, making it easier to drop if results disappoint, but its fit with the firm's bread range still argues for persistence.

Because the firm has publicly presented this poppy-seed stollen as a flagship and showcased its gold award, dropping it would visibly write off central investments and expose a mistake, so escalation strongly predicts keeping it.
